video_title: Ep. 114.26 Tom Tolbert Show | Special Guest: Steve Kerr!

quotes.speaker: Tom Tolbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors struggling to penetrate the paint without Steph Curry
quotes.excerpt: I think the first six and a half minutes, you guys touched the paint twice.
quotes.quote: I think the first six and a half minutes, you guys touched the paint twice. That's it. And I want to say barely touched the paint. One was Zubac got to the paint and got fouled, got to the free throw line. And the other one he barely got to the paint, passed it off to Horford, he missed the shot. But other than that, it was just all passing around the perimeter. Now that's what happened, Steph, right? That's what happened to a veteran out there that handles the ball the time can help guys with. How much of that was just maybe guys having to do more than they're capable, not capable, but more than they're used to doing because they don't have their star out there with them?

quotes.speaker: Steve Kerr
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Kerr explains Warriors' offensive spacing issues without Steph Curry
quotes.excerpt: starting Allen and Draymond together, you don't really get a roll man to the rim
quotes.quote: I think some of it is that, just adapting to playing without Steph. And then some of it, honestly, my lineup combination has to change. I think starting Allen and Draymond together, you don't really get a roll man to the rim to pull the defense in when you're running pick and roll. So we were popping on all the pick and rolls, which is fine if you can generate an advantage from the initial screen, because then you move the ball and somebody can attack a close out and you're getting the ball into the paint that way. But we weren't setting good screens, we weren't generating any advantages. So it was all just one-on-one. And if it's one-on-one like that, the only guy in the starting lineup who can play that way is Yax. And that's putting too much pressure on him.

quotes.speaker: Steve Kerr
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Kerr on Brandon Podziemski's role and development
quotes.excerpt: he's killing it. But it doesn't mean he's ready to take on the entire offensive load

text_blocks.speaker: Tom Tolbert
text_blocks.text: And not only Steph being out, it's a bad time for Brandon Williams to be out too, because he's a, I mean, he is a paint touch unto himself. Like he doesn't even need any help to get to the paint. That's right? He's like so quick, but that's what he does and it hurts not to have him because now you're asking guys to do things that maybe they don't have to do all the time and you're not quite as comfortable doing those things.

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Kerr
text_blocks.text: Totally. Totally. Yeah, so it's just part of the season every year is dealing with injuries and sometimes a bunch of them come at once. And, you know, for us this year, it's about surviving the first half of the season until we get Jimmy and Moses back. So when you already have some guys out and then you miss a couple of more guys, it really exposes things. And I think that's part of what's happening right now. So that means it's all that much more important to execute and be really sharp with your screen setting, with your cutting, all that with the spacing. So we've got to be better execution-wise and I've got to figure out some different combinations to try to get the ball into the paint more. 14 games in, when you look at what he's done, what he's accomplished, it's incredible. He's killing it. But it doesn't mean he's ready to take on the entire offensive load for a team, you know, missing Jimmy Butler and Steph Curry and all the other guys we're missing. It's just a lot.

quotes.speaker: Steve Kerr
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Kerr on managing losing streaks and mental approach
quotes.excerpt: if as a coach, you're up all night because of a decision that you made, all that is ego
quotes.quote: Took me a long time and I'm not sure I ever completely got past that. But you know, the biggest challenge I always had was if I had several bad games in a row, trying to get out of that rut. And Phil Jackson was great for for me in that regard. He introduced our team to meditation and mindfulness and I started reading books. My favorite book still to this day for an athlete is called The Inner Game of Tennis and a friend of mine gave me that book and it's about the mind-body connection and allowing your your body to do what it what it can do without your mind getting in the way. So I I I needed a lot of that help because I was I was just too hard on myself all the time. And so, you know, eventually I kind of realize you have to accept failure. It's part of it, you know, everybody fails. Even even Steph, Michael Jordan, even the greatest players ever are going to fail. And it's how you respond to that and the confidence that you bring to the next game that's the most important thing. If as a coach, you're up all night because of a decision that you made, all that is ego.

quotes.speaker: Steve Kerr
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Kerr on coaching and player pressure
quotes.excerpt: you can't take it on yourself and get, you know, start worrying about, what are people going to say about me
quotes.quote: I think the biggest thing is you have to recognize what the players are going through. You can't take it on yourself and get, you know, start worrying about, what are people going to say about me, you know, as a coach. You have to recognize that the players are the ones who are on the court feeling all the pressure and and going through, you know, what I used to go through as a player. So I have to recognize that and give them confidence and and give them something they can hang their hats on to to to improve the rhythm and the flow and and help them find their confidence again.

quotes.speaker: Steve Kerr
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Kerr on the Warriors' lineup and spacing challenges
quotes.excerpt: we were anticipating that he would play a lot more four rather than five
quotes.quote: You know what I think has happened because we did talk about it a lot in the summer, we were anticipating that he would play a lot more four rather than five. You know, we were anticipating that Kristaps would be our starting five and that Al Horford would come in behind Kristaps and Dray would play a lot more four which would have put him in the corners more. Um, he's been at the top of the floor a lot more as the five facilitating, dribble handoffs and ball screens. And um, you know, he's been he's played almost exclusively at the the five and um, so it kind of changes everything. But we have to examine the this stuff. As I mentioned earlier, like we we got to look at at playing him, you know, as a four next to Bassi, you know, Bassi rolling or Gram EK. We we've got to get a roller to the rim to to create more paint presence, more paint touches, uh, better screening out there. If we do that, that'll move Draymond to the corner more and that's where we're going to need him uh to rise up and shoot a three.

quotes.speaker: Steve Kerr
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Kerr on Jimmy Butler's impact on the team
quotes.excerpt: just by adding Jimmy Butler, we became a top five offense and defense
quotes.quote: Well, I think about when we traded for Jimmy Butler, you know, a year and a half ago, whatever it was, two years ago almost now. And we're floundering, you know, along, we're at 500, um, you know, middle of the pack both offensively and defensively. We add him, I guess it's in February, and for the last 30 games of the year, just by adding Jimmy Butler, we became a top five offense and defense. And nothing else changed. But you add a guy like that, whether it's Jimmy or Steph or, you know, name name whoever you want around the league who's that caliber player, the puzzle just falls into place, you know, the the pieces just fit and all of a sudden, you know, Jimmy Butler is going downhill, drawing two, swinging the ball and you're getting a wide open three instead of a contested three. That shot's more likely to go in, which means they're taking it out of the net, which means your defense is set up. So you're exactly right. I mean, when you can play off of a star, the the game gets way easier for every single player and then the whole team just gets better at both ends.

quotes.speaker: Steve Kerr
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Kerr on defensive strategy and foul rules
quotes.excerpt: if the ball's up in the air and your guy's going to get it, just commit pass interference
quotes.quote: Well, uh, Frank Vogel's a great uh basketball coach, great defensive coach and I think of the first or second day of training camp, we went over uh this exact situation, what our foul rules are, you know, if we're going to take the foul, you know, he has one, he calls pass interference, you know, like like if the ball's up in the air and your guy's going to get it, just commit pass interference, just go for the ball and run right through him because uh it won't there's no way there there can be three free throws, you know. And uh so he has kind of a series of rules and and um, so we've instituted those rules and we've practiced it a couple times since. Uh, but even then, like you, um, you know, it's it's it can be hit or miss, you know, we've fouled a couple times, um, over the years, up three where they called it on the shot. And, and so that's obviously a mistake, but um, you try your best to handle those situations and I think a big part of coaching is preparing your guys for those situations and you try to win more than you lose.

quotes.speaker: Steve Kerr
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Kerr on Cooper Flagg's development
quotes.excerpt: he's phenomenal. I mean, it's crazy that he's only, is he 19 still?
quotes.quote: Uh, he's phenomenal. I mean, it's crazy that he's only, is he 19 still? I think he's still 19. He's not even 20 yet. So well-rounded, uh, at both ends. He's added the mid-range shot this year. Um, he's just, he seems to have an answer for everything. Um, it's just advanced beyond his years. He's, he's incredible.
